### iam-identity-center-abac-attributes-as-session-tags

**Claim.** For attribute-based access control, IAM Identity Center passes selected user attributes from the identity source to the accessed account as session tags, which policies reference with the aws:PrincipalTag condition key.

**Write it as.** `sent as session tags` · `existing attributes in the users' identity source`

**Scope.** attributes for access control in IAM Identity Center.

> "You can assign users to workloads in AWS based on existing attributes in the users' identity source."
> — [Attributes for access control](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/attributesforaccesscontrol.html)

> "When IAM Identity Center passes these attributes to the account, they are sent as session tags that you can reference using the `aws:PrincipalTag/{{tag-key}}` condition key in all relevant AWS IAM policy types."
> — [Attributes for access control](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/attributesforaccesscontrol.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### iam-identity-center-abac-fewer-permission-sets

**Claim.** With ABAC in IAM Identity Center, user attributes from any identity source act as tags, so users who share one permission set get access only to resources with matching tags, and a change of the attribute in the corporate directory changes access without permission updates in AWS.

**Write it as.** `these attributes are called tags` · `only to the AWS resources with matching tags` · `without requiring any permissions updates in AWS`

**Scope.** ABAC with IAM Identity Center.

> "You can use IAM Identity Center to manage access to your AWS resources across multiple AWS accounts using user attributes that come from any IAM Identity Center identity source. In AWS, these attributes are called tags. Using user attributes as tags in AWS helps you simplify the process of creating fine-grained permissions in AWS and ensures that your workforce gets access only to the AWS resources with matching tags."
> — [Attribute-based access control](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/abac.html)

> "When Bob signs in next time, he will automatically get access to the project resources of his new team without requiring any permissions updates in AWS."
> — [Attribute-based access control](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/abac.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### iam-identity-center-admin-only-from-primary-region

**Claim.** IAM Identity Center supports most administrative functions only from the primary Region, including the external IdP connection, user and group synchronization, and creating and assigning permission sets; applications are managed in the Region where they were created.

**Write it as.** `most administrative functions only from the primary Region` · `Region where the application was created`

**Scope.** per IAM Identity Center instance.

> "IAM Identity Center supports most administrative functions only from the primary Region. This includes the connection to an external identity provider, synchronization of users and groups, and the creation and assignment of permission sets to users and groups. In contrast, the management of applications and their assignments must take place in the IAM Identity Center Region where the application was created."
> — [Resiliency design and Regional behavior](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/resiliency-regional-behavior.html)

### iam-identity-center-users-get-temporary-credentials

**Claim.** Users in IAM Identity Center are different from IAM users: IAM users have long-term credentials, while IAM Identity Center users get temporary credentials that are generated every time they sign in, which AWS recommends as a security best practice.

**Write it as.** `IAM users are granted long-term credentials` · `are granted temporary credentials` · `generated every time you sign in`

**Scope.** IAM Identity Center users.

> "IAM users are granted long-term credentials to AWS resources. Users in IAM Identity Center are granted temporary credentials. We recommend that you use temporary credentials as a security best practice for accessing your AWS accounts because these credentials are generated every time you sign in."
> — [Getting IAM Identity Center user credentials for the AWS CLI or AWS SDKs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/howtogetcredentials.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### iam-identity-center-wa-customer-rotates-scim-tokens-and-certificates

**Claim.** The customer is responsible for rotating SCIM access tokens and the certificates that support identity federation.

**Write it as.** `the rotation of SCIM access tokens` · `rotating the certificates supporting your identity federation`

**Scope.** external identity provider federation.

> "Additionally, you are responsible for rotating the certificates supporting your identity federation."
> — [SEC02-BP04 Rely on a centralized identity provider](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_identities_identity_provider.html)

> "You are responsible for handling the rotation of SCIM access tokens as described in the Automatic provisioning documentation."
> — [SEC02-BP04 Rely on a centralized identity provider](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_identities_identity_provider.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### iam-identity-center-wa-remove-iam-users-after-federation

**Claim.** After workforce federation is in place, the security pillar says to identify and remove IAM users, IAM groups and long-lived credentials that are no longer needed; an SCP can help prevent the creation of new IAM users and groups so that access to AWS is through federated identities.

**Write it as.** `long-lived user credentials (passwords and access keys)` · `prevent the creation of new IAM users` · `access to AWS is via federated identities`

**Scope.** workforce users federated to AWS.

> "You should identify and remove IAM groups, IAM users, and long-lived user credentials (passwords and access keys) that are no longer needed in your AWS accounts."
> — [SEC02-BP04 Rely on a centralized identity provider](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_identities_identity_provider.html)

> "You can apply a Service Control Policy (SCP) to your organization that helps prevent the creation of new IAM users and groups, enforcing that access to AWS is via federated identities."
> — [SEC02-BP04 Rely on a centralized identity provider](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_identities_identity_provider.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### iam-identity-center-wa-two-federation-approaches

**Claim.** The security pillar names two levels for federating workforce users to AWS: direct federation to each AWS account with IAM, or IAM Identity Center for single sign-on to multiple AWS accounts in an AWS organization.

**Write it as.** `direct federation to each AWS account` · `single sign-on to multiple AWS accounts` · `directly to each AWS account`

**Scope.** workforce users accessing AWS.

> "You can grant AWS access to your workforce users by federating from your centralized identity provider to AWS at two levels: direct federation to each AWS account or federating to multiple accounts in your AWS organization."
> — [SEC02-BP04 Rely on a centralized identity provider](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_identities_identity_provider.html)

> "Use IAM Identity Center to enable single sign-on to multiple AWS accounts in your AWS organization by federating with your identity provider."
> — [SEC02-BP04 Rely on a centralized identity provider](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_identities_identity_provider.html)

> "Use IAM to connect your identity provider directly to each AWS account, enabling federated fine-grained access."
> — [SEC02-BP04 Rely on a centralized identity provider](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_identities_identity_provider.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### iam-identity-center-wa-workforce-centralized-idp

**Claim.** The Well-Architected security pillar (SEC02-BP04) says to rely on an identity provider that manages workforce identities (employees and contractors) in a centralized place.

**Write it as.** `rely on an identity provider` · `manage identities in a centralized place`

**Scope.** workforce identities.

> "For workforce identities (employees and contractors), rely on an identity provider that allows you to manage identities in a centralized place."
> — [SEC02-BP04 Rely on a centralized identity provider](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_identities_identity_provider.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### iam-identity-center-workforce-sso-to-accounts-and-applications

**Claim.** IAM Identity Center gives employees single sign-on from an existing identity provider to user-facing AWS applications and to the AWS Management Console, including the AWS accounts assigned to them.

**Write it as.** `single sign-on experience of your employees` · `including any AWS accounts that are assigned`

**Scope.** workforce single sign-on to AWS accounts and AWS applications.

> "IAM Identity Center helps you configure the single sign-on experience of your employees from your existing identity provider to user-facing AWS applications, such as Amazon Q and Amazon SageMaker AI, and to the AWS Management Console, including any AWS accounts that are assigned to your employees."
> — [Choosing an AWS identity service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/decision-guides/latest/decision-guides/identity-on-aws-how-to-choose.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.
